title: Extract normality and G-delta halves of Munkres Lemma 40.1 into named step lemmas (Nagata-Smirnov)
intent: Reduce Munkres Lemma 40.1 — `regular with a sigma-locally-finite basis \<Longrightarrow> normal \<and> every closed set is G-delta` — to two named step lemmas whose proofs were lifted out of the conjunction: `Lemma_40_1_step3` proves the normality half and `Lemma_40_1_step2` the G-delta half, so the parent closes in four lines by applying both to the shared hReg/hBasis/hCLF context and letting `argo` assemble the conjunction.
also_known_as: lift a have into a standalone lemma

parent.name: Lemma_40_1
parent.statement: top1_normal_on X TX \<and> (\<forall>A. closedin_on X TX A \<longrightarrow> top1_G_delta_on X TX A)

children.name: Lemma_40_1_step2
children.statement: closedin_on X TX A \<Longrightarrow> top1_G_delta_on X TX A (under the same hReg/hBasis/hCLF)
children.closed_by: Lemma_40_1_step1 (line 4649) decomposes the open complement W = X - A into U n with cl(U n) \<subseteq> W and W = \<Union>n. U n; then V n = X - cl(U n) gives A = \<Inter>n. V n, and the goal closes by unfolding top1_G_delta_on_def and apply (rule exI[where x=V]) by satx

children.name: Lemma_40_1_step3
children.statement: top1_normal_on X TX (under the same hReg/hBasis/hCLF)
children.closed_by: unfolds top1_normal_on_def, then the Theorem 32.1 shrinking argument: Lemma_40_1_step1 applied twice (lines 4798, 4811) to X - D and X - C, define U'_n / V'_n by subtracting finite unions of closures, closedin_on_finite_Union (4854, 4891) makes those unions closed, and a WLOG m \<le> n case split closes the disjointness of UU and VV

applicability.goal_shape: A conjunction goal `P \<and> Q` over a shared hypothesis context (here `top1_regular_on X TX`, `basis_for X \<B> TX`, `top1_sigma_locally_finite_family_on X TX \<B>`), where each conjunct has a long proof that reuses the same assumptions verbatim; the parent proof is then just `using lemmaP lemmaQ by argo`.
applicability.use_when: the two conjuncts are independent (neither needs the other) and each is long enough to deserve its own lemma; both restate the same hypotheses, so the parent can instantiate each with a single `[OF hReg hBasis hCLF]`.
applicability.avoid_when: the two halves share a genuinely intermediate construction — extract that shared part first (as Lemma_40_1_step1 is here) rather than duplicating it in both children; or the conjunction is so short that one proof with `intro conjI` is clearer than two lemmas.

claims.claim: The parent `Lemma_40_1` is closed in four proof lines (5069-5072) by `using Lemma_40_1_step3[OF hReg hBasis hCLF]` and `Lemma_40_1_step2[OF hReg hBasis hCLF]` followed by `by argo`, with no other proof step.

Each child is a self-contained `lemma ... qed` in the same file that closes on its own, and the region 4369-5072 (the parent, both children, and the two context lemmas) contains no `sorry`, `oops` or `admit`.
claims.evidence: https://github.com/JUrban/isa_top_autoform1/blob/90d108779e83453e9cae2f55b513246e1cc044e0/tst/Top1_Ch5_8.thy#L4626-L4704 and https://github.com/JUrban/isa_top_autoform1/blob/90d108779e83453e9cae2f55b513246e1cc044e0/tst/Top1_Ch5_8.thy#L4756-L5062; grep for `sorry|oops|admit` over lines 4369-5072 returns no match (the file's such markers are all at line 12322 or later)

claims.claim: Below the parent there is a chain of project lemmas of depth 2: `Lemma_40_1_step2` closes by applying `Lemma_40_1_step1` (line 4649), and `Lemma_40_1_step3` closes by applying `Lemma_40_1_step1` twice (lines 4798 and 4811), so both branches are `Lemma_40_1 -> (step2 | step3) -> step1`.

The authors label the decomposition by step and tie it to the textbook: the section header reads '\S40 The Nagata-Smirnov Metrization Theorem' (line 4367), the provenance comment reads '(** from \S40 Lemma 40.1 [top1.tex:5675] **)' (line 4372), and the `text` blocks name each step — 'Step 1 of Lemma 40.1: open set decomposition' (4373), 'Step 2 of Lemma 40.1: closed sets are G-delta' (4625), 'Step 3 of Lemma 40.1: normality via the Theorem 32.1 technique' (4706).
The shape is a measurement: a 9-line parent (5064-5072) whose 4-line proof body delegates 386 lines to the two children (step2 = 4626-4704 = 79 lines; step3 = 4756-5062 = 307 lines).

metrics.how_counted: parent = 5064-5072 (9 lines); glue (proof body) = 5069-5072 (4); children = 4626-4704 (79) and 4756-5062 (307); Lemma_40_1 reused at 6105 and 6107 by Theorem_40_3

consequences: The move turns one conjunction goal into two named obligations (normality, and closed-implies-G-delta) that each restate the three shared hypotheses hReg/hBasis/hCLF verbatim. The parent's `using` step relies on the two children having exactly those three `assumes` in the same order, so a child that adds or drops a hypothesis breaks the `[OF hReg hBasis hCLF]` template. The two children are independent of each other (each calls the shared open-decomposition `Lemma_40_1_step1`, never its sibling), so they can be proved in parallel. The real difficulty is not removed but pushed one level down into `Lemma_40_1_step1` (248 lines); if that shared lemma is wrong or too weak, both children fail together. Downstream, `Theorem_40_3` (the Nagata-Smirnov metrization theorem) consumes `Lemma_40_1` twice (lines 6105 and 6107), so the decomposition's statement must stay exactly the one that theorem needs.
